modules.title: Ashby: selection, regulation, and variety
modules.summary: Challoner reconstructs Ashby through selected variables, transformations, constraints, and regulation. Read the general definitions before the specialised regulatory claims. The good-regulator result has formal conditions; it is not a licence to assume every manager has an adequate model.
modules.distinction: A system selected for inquiry is not identical with the object being investigated.
concepts: Variety counts distinguishable possibilities; information concerns eliminated alternatives.
Regulation concerns the effects of disturbances on specified essential variables.
Ultrastability changes parameters when essential variables leave their limits.
The good-regulator proposition is presented with stated mathematical qualifications.
modules.author: John A Challoner
modules.status: All pages read; secondary reconstruction, not a new verification of every original citation

modules.title: Bhaskar: mechanisms in open systems
modules.summary: Challoner distinguishes what exists, what happens, and what is experienced. Mechanisms can operate without producing an isolated regularity. Social structures and agency are interdependent but distinct; this does not turn every retrospective explanation into a demonstrated mechanism.
modules.distinction: Causal openness means interacting mechanisms, whereas material openness means exchange across a boundary.
concepts: Causal powers concern capacities of structured entities; emergence involves differentiated levels.
Multiple mechanisms can jointly shape an outcome in an open causal system.
Emergent powers depend on underlying organisation without being reduced to it.
Social structures depend on activity while conditioning the agency that reproduces or transforms them.
modules.author: John A Challoner
modules.status: All pages read; secondary reconstruction, not a new verification of every original citation

modules.title: Bogdanov: organisation and its changing boundaries
modules.summary: Challoner presents complexes through activities and resistances, with organisation as a practical relation. Joining, separation, selection, and changing boundaries matter to persistence. Egression and degression distinguish concentration around a centre from stabilising forms.
modules.distinction: Least relative resistance concerns a specified disturbance; it is not a universal weakest-link slogan.
concepts: A complex is considered through activities, resistances, conjunction, and separation.
Persistence can involve continuing activity rather than an absence of change.
A tektological boundary arises within organisational interactions.
Egression concerns organisation around a centre; degression concerns relatively stable supporting forms.
modules.author: John A Challoner
modules.status: All pages read; secondary reconstruction, not a new verification of every original citation

modules.title: Prigogine: order under non-equilibrium conditions
modules.summary: Challoner separates equilibrium, stationary states, and far-from-equilibrium behaviour. Sustained exchange, instability, and fluctuations help explain dissipative structures in specified physical systems. These propositions require separate argument and evidence before application to organisations.
modules.distinction: Stationarity can coexist with irreversible processes and flows; stationarity is not thermodynamic equilibrium.
concepts: Matter or energy exchange can maintain non-equilibrium conditions.
A dissipative structure persists under non-equilibrium conditions maintained by exchange.
Instability can produce branching alternatives in a system’s development.
Fluctuations can be amplified under particular non-linear, non-equilibrium conditions.
modules.author: John A Challoner
modules.status: All pages read; secondary reconstruction, not a new verification of every original citation

modules.title: Bertalanffy: organisation, openness, and equifinality
modules.summary: Challoner distinguishes organised relations from additive collections and cross-domain isomorphism from reduction to one discipline. Open-system accounts of organisms support specific claims about steady states and equifinality. Neither term means every route always reaches the same outcome.
modules.distinction: A steady state sustained by flows differs from closed-system equilibrium.
concepts: Open systems exchange matter and can maintain steady states away from equilibrium.
Different initial conditions can lead to the same final state under specified open-system conditions.
Cross-domain formal correspondences do not remove substantive differences between domains.
Organisation depends on relations that an additive account of parts can miss.
modules.author: John A Challoner
modules.status: All pages read; secondary reconstruction, not a new verification of every original citation

new_concepts: Capacities attributed to structured entities in critical realist explanation. A proposed capacity still needs an account of its operation and evidence; observing an outcome alone does not establish its mechanism.

A system in which several mechanisms can act together, so an observed outcome need not express any one mechanism in isolation. This critical realist use of openness differs from a claim about material exchange.

A distinction between social conditions and the actions that reproduce or transform them. Their interdependence does not make the concepts interchangeable or settle who can act in a particular setting.
In Challoner’s reconstruction of Bogdanov, an organisational complex is investigated through activities and resistances, including the processes that join or separate complexes.
Persistence sustained through continuing activity and changing relations in a tektological account. The domain qualifier matters: the term is not used here as a synonym for thermodynamic equilibrium.

Bogdanov’s distinction between organisation around a centre and relatively stable supporting forms, as presented in Challoner’s researcher module. These are analytical distinctions rather than recommended management structures.

A system that exchanges matter across its boundary; thermodynamic accounts also attend to energy exchange. Material openness is distinct from Bhaskar’s causal openness and from an invitation to organisational participation.

An organised physical pattern sustained under non-equilibrium conditions through continuing exchanges. Application to social or organisational life needs its own mechanism and evidence rather than resemblance alone.

A branching of possible behaviours as conditions change in a dynamical account. The Prigogine route concerns specified non-linear systems; the word alone is not an explanation of a social turning point.

The possibility of reaching the same final state from different initial conditions in specified open-system accounts. It is a conditional claim, not a guarantee that any intervention can achieve any desired outcome.

A specified correspondence of formal structure across domains. A useful correspondence preserves identified relations; it does not establish that the compared systems have the same material properties or social purposes.

Organisation considered through relations among components and their effects. The concept supports inquiry into what a decomposition preserves or loses; it does not imply that every whole possesses the same kind of organisation.

Matter or energy transferred across a physical system boundary. In Challoner’s Prigogine module, either kind of exchange enters the account of non-equilibrium organisation; energy exchange alone does not establish material openness.
concept_edges: In the module’s regulatory setting, blocking disturbance variety protects specified essential variables.
Ultrastability adds parameter change when essential variables leave acceptable limits.
The tektological account treats boundary formation as part of organisational interaction.
The module’s dissipative structures require sustained exchanges under non-equilibrium conditions; openness alone is insufficient.
The module locates equifinality within specified open-system conditions, not an unrestricted management claim.

principles: State what a map is for
A diagram is an argument made for a purpose and audience. Record its boundary, omissions, date, author, and intended use.
Systems thinking, complexity, and cybernetics have overlapping histories and diverse internal positions. Do not turn a convenient region into a closed disciplinary border.
A line might record citation, teaching, collaboration, a formal dependence, or an author’s interpretation. Direction, evidence, and scope must travel with the line.
Readers should be able to change focus, filters, scale, and representation without losing their place. A textual account must remain available alongside a visual one.
Attribution is more than attaching a famous name. Attend to translation, borrowing, exclusion, recovery, and the conditions under which a practice is shared.
Coverage reflects access, languages, source selection, and editorial effort. A sparse region is a research question, not proof of a peripheral tradition.
A shared word or similar shape does not establish equivalence. Keep domain-specific meanings and disagreements visible; justify each proposed correspondence.
Expose corrections and uncertain interpretations. Preserve source maps separately from the atlas claims that further evidence may justify.
